reason: OEO's motor gasoline is road gasoline with its blending components; the group is close to it, not exact, because the 10-K names the group without defining it.
Reformulated gasoline is a regulated kind of motor gasoline; OEO has no class for it.
OEO's motor gasoline includes blending components destined for finished motor gasoline.
ULSD is one grade of gas/diesel oil.
Both are kerosene-type fuel for aviation turbine engines.
OEO's kerosene also covers jet fuel, which this scheme keeps apart.
OEO's heating oil is gas diesel oil for heating and similar uses; No. 2 fuel oil is the heating grade.
Commercial propane is a kind of LPG; OEO has no propane class.
Butane sold as LPG fits OEO's definition, which names propane and butane.
Propylene is a hydrocarbon; OEO has no propylene class.
Xylene is a hydrocarbon; OEO has no xylene class.
Benzene is a hydrocarbon; OEO has no benzene class.
Toluene is a hydrocarbon; OEO has no toluene class.
Cumene is a hydrocarbon; OEO has no cumene class.
Fuel-grade coke is one grade of petroleum coke.
Anode-grade coke is one grade of petroleum coke.
OEO has no fuel oil class (OEO issue 1958); a residual fuel oil is a mineral oil product.
Renewable diesel is a diesel fuel; OEO has no renewable diesel class.
Renewable diesel is a liquid biofuel; OEO has no renewable diesel class.
